config.title: Controlled DatePicker

intro.title: Controlled DatePicker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a controlled DatePicker component in Angular. You will learn how to manage a selected date using Angular's reactive forms and two-way data binding. The core concept involves creating a form control to handle the date value and synchronizing it with the user interface. You will use key Angular constructs like FormControl, DatePipe, and template binding to implement the component. By the end, you will have a functional DatePicker that updates and reflects the date state predictably.
intro.usecase: Controlled DatePickers are essential in Angular forms where you need precise validation and data synchronization, such as in booking systems for flights or hotels where check-in/check-out dates must be validated. They appear in dashboards for filtering time-series data, like selecting date ranges in analytics tools to view specific performance metrics. In enterprise applications, controlled DatePickers ensure form data consistency when integrated with backend APIs, such as in HR systems for selecting employee leave dates with business rule enforcement.

objectives: Implement a controlled DatePicker component in Angular using TypeScript
Configure two-way data binding between the DatePicker and a component property
Initialize and manipulate date values using Angular's reactive forms approach
Apply validation rules to ensure selected dates meet specific criteria
Construct a template that renders the DatePicker with proper event handling
Integrate the controlled DatePicker into a parent component with data synchronization
Update the component state based on user interactions with the DatePicker

steps.title: Import Component, FormsModule, and DatePickerModule
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core', FormsModule from '@angular/forms', and DatePickerModule from '@syncfusion/ej2-angular-calendars'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path. Separate multiple imports with commas.
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules and date picker library are imported, enabling component creation and form handling.
successCriteria: Component, FormsModule, and DatePickerModule are imported from their respective modules.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some imports are missing. Make sure to import Component, FormsModule, and DatePickerModule from their correct module paths.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or incomplete. Check that you're importing Component from '@angular/core', FormsModule from '@angular/forms', and DatePickerModule from '@syncfusion/ej2-angular-calendars'.

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction: Create a class named DatePickerComponent and decorate it with @Component, setting the selector to 'app-date-picker' and using an inline template with a simple placeholder.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component. Provide a selector and a template property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DatePickerComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator, ready to be extended with logic and UI.
successCriteria: DatePickerComponent class exists, decorated with @Component, with selector 'app-date-picker' and a template property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the class is named DatePickerComponent and uses the @Component decorator with the correct selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a class named DatePickerComponent with the @Component decorator, selector, and template.

steps.title: Initialize the selectedDate state property
steps.instruction: Inside the component class, add a property named 'selectedDate' of type 'Date' and initialize it with a new Date object.
steps.hint: In Angular, component properties are declared directly in the class. Use 'selectedDate: Date = new Date();' to create and initialize the property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has a 'selectedDate' property that holds the current date value, ready to be bound to the date picker.
successCriteria: The component class contains a 'selectedDate' property of type 'Date' initialized with 'new Date()'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check that it's named 'selectedDate', has type 'Date', and is initialized with 'new Date()'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class should have a property named 'selectedDate' of type 'Date' initialized with 'new Date()'.

steps.title: Define the onDateChange handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the DatePickerComponent class, add a method named onDateChange that takes a date parameter and updates the selectedDate property with the new date value.
steps.hint: The method should have a parameter (like 'date') and assign this.date = date inside its body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can handle date changes and update the component's state.
successCriteria: The DatePickerComponent class contains a method named onDateChange that takes a date parameter and assigns it to the selectedDate property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check that it's named exactly 'onDateChange' and properly updates the selectedDate property with the date parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onDateChange method is missing or doesn't correctly update the selectedDate property. Make sure to add a method that takes a date parameter and assigns it to this.selectedDate.

steps.title: Add the component template structure
steps.instruction: Inside the component decorator's template property, add a div container with a class of 'container' to hold the date picker and display.
steps.hint: The template property currently contains an empty string. Replace it with a div element that has a class attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now has a div container element with a class attribute.
successCriteria: The template property contains a div element with a class attribute set to 'container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div, but make sure it has the class attribute set to 'container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template property should contain a div element with a class attribute.

steps.title: Add the date picker control to the template
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add an <ejs-datepicker> element with the [(ngModel)] attribute bound to the selectedDate property.
steps.hint: Use Angular's two-way data binding syntax [(ngModel)] to connect the date picker to the component's selectedDate property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Adding a bound input element
<input [(ngModel)]="userName" placeholder="Enter name">
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a date picker control that will be bound to the component's selectedDate property.
successCriteria: The template includes an <ejs-datepicker> element with [(ngModel)]="selectedDate" attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the date picker element, but make sure it has the [(ngModel)] attribute bound to selectedDate.
steps.feedbackWrong: The date picker element is missing or incorrectly implemented. Add <ejs-datepicker> with [(ngModel)]="selectedDate" to the template.

steps.title: Bind the date picker to selectedDate using ngModel
steps.instruction: In the template, add the [(ngModel)] binding to the date picker element to connect it with the selectedDate property.
steps.hint: Use the two-way binding syntax [(ngModel)]="selectedDate" on the date picker element.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: binding an input to a property -->
<input type="text" [(ngModel)]="username" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The date picker will be two-way bound to the selectedDate property, allowing user selections to update the component state.
successCriteria: The date picker element has the [(ngModel)] binding with selectedDate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct two-way binding syntax [(ngModel)] with the selectedDate property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The date picker isn't properly bound. Check that you're using [(ngModel)]="selectedDate" on the date picker element.

steps.title: Wire the change event to onDateChange handler
steps.instruction: Add a (change) event binding to the existing date picker input that calls the onDateChange method with $event.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (event)="handler($event)". The $event object will contain the new date value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a change event to a method
<input type="text" (change)="handleTextChange($event)" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The date picker will now trigger the onDateChange method whenever its value changes, updating the component state.
successCriteria: The date picker input has a (change) event binding that calls onDateChange with $event.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct event binding syntax and passing $event to the handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The date picker doesn't have the correct event binding. Check the syntax and ensure you're calling onDateChange with $event.

steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the date picker that displays the current selectedDate value using Angular interpolation.

Use the

Selected date: {{ selectedDate }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the selected date value in a paragraph below the date picker control.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists below the date picker that displays the selectedDate value using interpolation syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the selectedDate value using interpolation syntax like {{ selectedDate }}.
steps.feedbackWrong:

steps.title: Add module imports to the main module
steps.instruction: In the main application module (typically app.module.ts), add FormsModule and DatePickerModule to the imports array.
steps.hint: Look for the @NgModule decorator in your app.module.ts file and update the imports array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main application module will have FormsModule and DatePickerModule properly imported, enabling the date picker component to work.
successCriteria: FormsModule and DatePickerModule are added to the imports array of the main application module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
